主要内容: By September 30, 34.5 million households in the U.S. will lose utility shutoff protections, according to a report by energy efficiency startup Carbon Switch. These protections were put in place during the coronavirus pandemic by state and local governments to prevent utility companies from disconnecting services like gas, electricity, and water due to nonpayment. However, many of these measures are set to expire soon, leaving millions without protection. Ten states have already had their orders expire, while the majority are set to end in August, September, and October. Meanwhile, 14 states never issued specific moratoriums, relying instead on utility companies to voluntarily keep power on for customers with overdue bills. Carbon Switch reports that 8 out of 10 of the nation's largest utility companies plan to return to normal operations by September 15, starting to cut off electricity and gas for overdue bills. Michael Thomas, founder and head researcher of Carbon Switch, warns of a 'tidal wave of utility shutoffs' due to high delinquency rates in some states, with as many as a third of households behind on payments. The report also highlights that low-income Americans, Black, and Hispanic households are disproportionately affected by utility shutoffs, with Black households earning less than 150% of the federal poverty level being twice as likely to have their electricity shut off compared to white families with similar incomes. As of September 30, 34.5 million households in the United States will lose utility shutoff protections. This means that many low-income families may face the risk of having their electricity, water, or telephone services disconnected. The National Consumer Law Center (NCLC) reports that only 1% of eligible households take advantage of bill assistance programs. However, there are several programs available to help those in need. The Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program (LIHEAP) is a federal program that assists low-income families with energy bills. Eligibility varies by state, but generally, a four-person household earning less than $36,400 qualifies. The National Energy Assistance Referral (NEAR) hotline can provide information on how to apply for LIHEAP. The Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF) program can also help with basic assistance and expenses related to housing, food, child care, and job training. Additionally, the Federal Communications Commission's Lifeline program offers discounted landline or cell phone service to low-income families. The status of utility moratoriums varies by state, with some expiring as early as May 14 and others expiring as late as September 30.

股票实体.名称: Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program (LIHEAP)
